2	 * Server-side retry utility for transient Neon/Postgres connection errors.
3	 *
4	 * Two presets are exposed:
5	 *   - `withDbRetry`        — generic capacity-class errors (3 attempts, 500ms base, exp. back-off + jitter).
6	 *   - `withColdStartRetry` — cold-start blips on the FIRST db.* call of a Lambda invocation
7	 *                            (1 retry, 50ms backoff). See ADR-009.
8	 *
9	 * Use `withColdStartRetry` ONLY around the first DB call in a hot Hono handler.
10	 * Do not wrap mutating queries that aren't idempotent. Real DB errors should
11	 * still 500 fast — these wrappers refuse to retry permanent failures (auth,
12	 * schema, syntax, constraint violations).
13	 */

15	import { safeErrorMessage } from '@/lib/safe-error-message';
16	import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs';
17	
18	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
19	// Error classification
20	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	
22	/** Patterns that indicate a transient, retryable failure. */
23	export const RETRYABLE_PATTERNS: ReadonlyArray<string | RegExp> = [
24	  // Neon cold-start / capacity
25	  'connection timeout',
26	  'Connection terminated unexpectedly',
27	  'sorry, too many clients already',
28	  'remaining connection slots are reserved',
29	  'could not translate host name',
30	  // Neon serverless HTTP/WebSocket bootstrap (cold-start blips surface here)
31	  'fetch failed',
32	  'terminating connection',
33	  // WebSocket transport (Neon serverless driver)
34	  'WebSocket was closed',
35	  'WebSocket is not open',
36	  // Generic TCP / TLS
37	  'ECONNRESET',
38	  'ECONNREFUSED',
39	  'ETIMEDOUT',
40	  'EPIPE',
41	  'EAI_AGAIN',
42	  /read ECONNRESET/,
43	  /Client has encountered a connection error/,
44	];
45	
46	/** Patterns that should NOT be retried (permanent failures). */
47	export const NON_RETRYABLE_PATTERNS: ReadonlyArray<string | RegExp> = [
48	  // Auth
49	  'password authentication failed',
50	  'no pg_hba.conf entry',
51	  // Schema / constraint
52	  'relation "',
53	  'column "',
54	  'duplicate key value violates unique constraint',
55	  'violates foreign key constraint',
56	  'violates not-null constraint',
57	  'violates check constraint',
58	  // Syntax
59	  'syntax error at or near',
60	  // Permission
61	  'permission denied',
62	];
63	
64	function matchesAny(
65	  message: string,
66	  patterns: ReadonlyArray<string | RegExp>,
67	): boolean {
68	  return patterns.some((p) =>
69	    typeof p === 'string' ? message.includes(p) : p.test(message),
70	  );
71	}
72	
73	/**
74	 * Determine whether an error is transient and worth retrying.
75	 *
76	 * Returns `true` only when the error message matches a known retryable
77	 * pattern AND does not match any non-retryable pattern. Uses
78	 * `safeErrorMessage` so plain-object errors thrown by Neon's serverless
79	 * driver (e.g. `{severity:'FATAL', code:'08006'}`) are inspected correctly
80	 * instead of becoming `[object Object]`.
81	 */
82	export function isRetryable(error: unknown): boolean {
83	  const message = safeErrorMessage(error);
84	  if (matchesAny(message, NON_RETRYABLE_PATTERNS)) return false;
85	  return matchesAny(message, RETRYABLE_PATTERNS);
86	}
87	
88	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	// Retry wrapper
90	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
91	
92	export interface BreadcrumbHint {
93	  /** Sentry tag value, e.g. `'squawks'`. */
94	  feature: string;
95	  /** Short label for the wrapped call, e.g. `'nextSquawkNumber'`. */
96	  op: string;
97	}
98	
99	export interface RetryOptions {
100	  /** Maximum number of attempts (including the first). @default 3 */
101	  maxAttempts?: number;
102	  /** Base delay in ms before the first retry. @default 500 */
103	  baseDelayMs?: number;
104	  /** Upper-bound delay in ms. @default 5000 */
105	  maxDelayMs?: number;
106	  /** Optional callback invoked before each retry. */
107	  onRetry?: (error: unknown, attempt: number, delayMs: number) => void;
108	  /**
109	   * When set, emits a Sentry breadcrumb on retry and on success-after-retry
110	   * so we can see retry rates in transaction context without paying for an
111	   * exception capture.
112	   */
113	  breadcrumb?: BreadcrumbHint;
114	}
115	
116	const DEFAULTS: Required<Omit<RetryOptions, 'onRetry' | 'breadcrumb'>> = {
117	  maxAttempts: 3,
118	  baseDelayMs: 500,
119	  maxDelayMs: 5_000,
120	};
121	
122	/**
123	 * Cold-start preset: 1 retry, 50 ms fixed backoff.
124	 *
125	 * The Neon serverless driver opens a fresh transport (WebSocket or HTTP fetch)
126	 * on the first db.* call of a Lambda invocation. Intermittent transport
127	 * failures during this bootstrap surface as `fetch failed` /
128	 * `Connection terminated unexpectedly` and resolve within tens of ms. A single
129	 * fast retry absorbs the blip without delaying real outage failures.
130	 */
131	export const COLD_START_DEFAULTS: Required<
132	  Omit<RetryOptions, 'onRetry' | 'breadcrumb'>
133	> = {
134	  maxAttempts: 2,
135	  baseDelayMs: 50,
136	  maxDelayMs: 50,
137	};
138	
139	/**
140	 * Execute `fn` with automatic retries for transient DB errors.
141	 *
142	 * ```ts
143	 * const rows = await withDbRetry(() => db.select().from(users));
144	 * ```
145	 *
146	 * For wrapping the FIRST db call of a hot Hono handler, prefer
147	 * `withColdStartRetry` (1 retry, 50 ms) — see ADR-009.
148	 */
149	export async function withDbRetry<T>(
150	  fn: () => Promise<T>,
151	  opts?: RetryOptions,
152	): Promise<T> {
153	  const { maxAttempts, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs } = { ...DEFAULTS, ...opts };
154	  let lastError: unknown;
155	
156	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
157	    try {
158	      const result = await fn();
159	      if (attempt > 1 && opts?.breadcrumb) {
160	        Sentry.addBreadcrumb({
161	          category: 'db.retry',
162	          message: `db.retry.success: ${opts.breadcrumb.feature}.${opts.breadcrumb.op}`,
163	          level: 'info',
164	          data: { attempts: attempt },
165	        });
166	      }
167	      return result;
168	    } catch (err) {
169	      lastError = err;
170	
171	      if (attempt === maxAttempts || !isRetryable(err)) {
172	        throw err;
173	      }
174	
175	      // Fixed-delay path when baseDelayMs === maxDelayMs (cold-start preset);
176	      // otherwise exponential back-off: base * 2^(attempt-1), capped at
177	      // maxDelayMs, with +-25% jitter.
178	      let delay: number;
179	      if (baseDelayMs === maxDelayMs) {
180	        delay = baseDelayMs;
181	      } else {
182	        const expDelay = Math.min(baseDelayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1), maxDelayMs);
183	        const jitter = expDelay * (0.75 + Math.random() * 0.5);
184	        delay = Math.round(jitter);
185	      }
186	
187	      if (opts?.breadcrumb) {
188	        Sentry.addBreadcrumb({
189	          category: 'db.retry',
190	          message: `db.retry: ${opts.breadcrumb.feature}.${opts.breadcrumb.op}`,
191	          level: 'warning',
192	          data: {
193	            attempt,
194	            delayMs: delay,
195	            error: safeErrorMessage(err),
196	          },
197	        });
198	      }
199	
200	      opts?.onRetry?.(err, attempt, delay);
201	
202	      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
203	    }
204	  }
205	
206	  // Should be unreachable, but satisfies TS control-flow analysis.
207	  throw lastError;
208	}
209	
210	/**
211	 * Cold-start retry preset for the first db.* call of a hot Hono handler.
212	 *
213	 * Equivalent to `withDbRetry(fn, { maxAttempts: 2, baseDelayMs: 50, ... })`
214	 * but with the defaults baked in so callsites stay terse. Always pass a
215	 * breadcrumb hint — the whole point is observability of retry rates.
216	 *
217	 * ```ts
218	 * const squawkNumber = await withColdStartRetry(
219	 *   () => nextSquawkNumber(orgId),
220	 *   { feature: 'squawks', op: 'nextSquawkNumber' },
221	 * );
222	 * ```
223	 */
224	export function withColdStartRetry<T>(
225	  fn: () => Promise<T>,
226	  breadcrumb: BreadcrumbHint,
227	): Promise<T> {
228	  return withDbRetry(fn, { ...COLD_START_DEFAULTS, breadcrumb });
229	}

content.text: The schema wants `slice` and `findings` at the top level directly, not nested under `input`.

findings.title: Row-Level Security tenant isolation is fully deployed at the DB but never activated by application code
findings.detail: Migration 0144 enables RLS with tenant_isolation/tenant_insert policies on ~80 tenant-scoped tables, gated on current_setting('app.flight_school_id') via get_current_flight_school_id(). The only application code that ever calls set_config('app.flight_school_id', ...) is setTenantContext() in src/lib/db-tenant-context.ts — and a repo-wide grep shows setTenantContext/clearTenantContext have zero callers anywhere in src/. Every real query therefore executes with app.flight_school_id unset (NULL). Cross-checked routes-stripe.ts: tenant scoping there is done entirely via explicit flightSchoolId !== callerOrgId checks in application code, not RLS.
findings.impact: The migration comment and function docstrings assert RLS is 'the mechanism that prevents cross-org data leakage,' but it is not wired up. Any application-code bug that omits a WHERE flight_school_id = ... filter has no DB-level backstop. This is exactly the class of incident ADR-002 exists to prevent, and the safety net is currently a no-op.
findings.recommendation: Either (1) wire setTenantContext/clearTenantContext into the actual request path (Hono middleware, per-request, before any query) and verify the connection pooling model actually preserves session-local GUCs per logical request (see next finding), or (2) if RLS is intentionally not used and app-layer WHERE clauses are the real control, remove/document the RLS migration and dead functions so nobody trusts a phantom backstop.

findings.title: Even if activated, setTenantContext's session GUC cannot be safely used with the shared connection Pool
findings.detail: db (src/lib/db.ts:59) is a lazy Drizzle client over a shared @neondatabase/serverless Pool (max 8 connections). setTenantContext calls db.execute(sql`SELECT set_config(..., true)`) — set_config with is_local=true is transaction-scoped and reverts on whichever physical connection serviced that call. Drizzle's pooled db.execute checks out an arbitrary connection per call; there's no pool.connect() + pinned client per logical request/transaction here. Even if setTenantContext were called, the next query for the same 'session' could land on a different pooled connection with no tenant context set, or inherit stale context left by a prior request that was never cleared.
findings.impact: RLS-via-session-GUC as currently structured is fundamentally unsafe under connection pooling: it can silently apply the wrong tenant's context to a query, or none at all. This is a correctness bug waiting to be exploited the moment someone 'fixes' the dead-code issue above by calling setTenantContext from middleware without also re-architecting connection handling.
findings.recommendation: If RLS is to be the real enforcement mechanism, tenant context must be set on a per-transaction basis using a pinned client (pool.connect() -> set_config -> run all tenant queries on that client -> release), or set at the start of every db.transaction() callback, never on the ambient pooled db. Otherwise keep RLS as documentation-only and rely solely on the application-level flightSchoolId checks that are actually doing the work today.

findings.title: check:tenant-guard CI gate is defined but never invoked by pre-push or CI workflows
findings.detail: scripts/check-tenant-write-guard.ts implements two real regression gates (derive-from-URL org guard, hardcoded PII roster) and is registered as npm run check:tenant-guard (package.json:42). Grepping .husky/pre-push and .github/workflows/*.yml for check:tenant-guard / check-tenant-write-guard returns no matches — the gate is not called from the pre-push hook or from any CI workflow.
findings.impact: The exact class of regression this script exists to catch (hardcoded roster, derive-from-URL missing org guard — both explicitly cited in the script's own header comment as prior incidents) can be reintroduced and merged without this check ever running.
findings.recommendation: Add npm run check:tenant-guard to .husky/pre-push (alongside the existing migration-journal check) and/or a CI workflow step, so it actually blocks the regressions it was built to catch.

findings.title: Soft-delete read filter helpers exist and are tested but have zero production callers
findings.detail: notDeleted()/liveAnd() (src/server/db/soft-delete.ts) are the designated shared filter for excluding soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) rows, per the file's own doc comment: 'the internal Hono routes and the repository layer do not [filter], so once soft-delete is rolled out, those reads would leak archived rows back into the UI.' A repo-wide grep for notDeleted( / liveAnd( outside the test file and definition file returns zero results.
findings.impact: 12 tables carry a deleted_at column (per drizzle/*.sql), implying soft-delete is at least partially rolled out at the schema level, but the documented required read-filter is not applied anywhere in application code. Archived/soft-deleted rows can surface in live queries and the UI.
findings.recommendation: Audit every table with a deleted_at column, confirm whether soft-delete is actually relied upon, and wire notDeleted/liveAnd into the corresponding repository read paths. If soft-delete isn't live yet, update the doc comment so it doesn't read as an already-broken guarantee.

findings.title: idempotency_keys table has no tenant scoping — global key namespace across all flight schools
findings.detail: The idempotency_keys table (drizzle/0142) has PK key varchar(255) with no flight_school_id/tenant column, and withIdempotency() (src/lib/idempotency.ts:9) looks up/stores purely by the caller-supplied key string with no tenant qualifier. If any caller derives the idempotency key from client-controllable or non-globally-unique input, one flight school's request could collide with another's key and receive a cached response containing a different tenant's data.
findings.impact: Cross-tenant response leakage if two different flight schools' requests ever produce the same idempotency key. Currently zero callers found for withIdempotency( outside its own definition, so not yet exploitable, but it is landmine dead code waiting for the first caller.
findings.recommendation: Add a flight_school_id column to idempotency_keys, include it in the lookup/insert WHERE and uniqueness constraint, and require callers to pass the tenant id explicitly. Compare to accounting_provider_idempotency_keys (drizzle/0346) which correctly scopes by owner_type, owner_id, provider, ... — follow that pattern.

Between the SELECT and the INSERT there is no lock/transaction — two concurrent requests with the same idempotency key will both see 'no existing row', both execute handler(), and race on the INSERT: the loser's real result is silently discarded and it returns cached: false with its own executed-but-orphaned result, not the winner's actual persisted response.

findings.detail: runSchemaDriftProbe() (src/lib/db-startup-probe.ts:114) runs at server startup, diffs live information_schema.columns against the Drizzle schema, and executes ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS directly against production — including dynamically creating enum types (ensureEnumType) — completely outside drizzle/*.sql + _journal.json.
